title: Daniel Radcliffe and the Art of Playing a "Weird Little Guy"
summary:
A film writer says has a fun way to see how far Daniel Radcliffe has come since the Harry Potter movies. In an opinion piece, the writer recommends the 2016 movie "Swiss Army Man," now on Netflix. Daniel Scheinert and Daniel Kwan, known as "the Daniels," wrote and directed it. They later made "Everything Everywhere All at Once." The writer calls the movie "absolutely wild in the best way."

The writer also uses the phrase "weird little guy." It describes an actor who can turn into strange, unusual characters. The writer says it is about a state of mind, not size. Radcliffe, the writer says, is a great example.

Since Harry Potter, Radcliffe has worked hard to avoid being tied to that role. His roles include a man who grows horns in "Horns" and a sneaky villain in "Now You See Me 2." He has also done stage work and won his first Tony Award for "Merrily We Roll Along." In 2026 he stars with Tracy Morgan in a comedy called "The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins."
why_it_matters: The article shows how an actor known for one famous role can try many different kinds of parts, and it gives readers ideas for what to watch.
